statement: For a discrete-time nonlinear state-space model with motion model $\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, \mathbf{w}_t)$ where $\mathbf{w}_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \mathbf{Q}_t)$ and observation model $\mathbf{z}_t = \mathbf{h}(\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{v}_t)$ where $\mathbf{v}_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \mathbf{R}_t)$, the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) linearizes $\mathbf{f}$ and $\mathbf{h}$ via first-order Taylor expansion around the current state estimates $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}$ (with $\mathbf{w}_t=0, \mathbf{v}_t=0$) to propagate and update a Gaussian belief $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t})$. Its prediction step is $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{f}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, 0)$, $\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1|t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}} \mathbf{Q}_t \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}^{\intercal}$, and its correction step is $\mathbf{K}_t = \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal}(\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}} \mathbf{R}_t \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}^{\intercal})^{-1}$, $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} + \mathbf{K}_t(\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{h}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, 0))$, $\mathbf{P}_{t|t} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_t \mathbf{H}_t)\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}$. (Note: the supplied excerpt of [arxiv:2406.06427] derives the linearization and Gaussian transition/observation densities in full, while referring the closed-form evaluation of the resulting linear-Gaussian integral and product in Eq. 38 to Section 8, which is not included in the excerpt.)

steps.text: Define the discrete-time non-linear motion model and non-linear observation model with Gaussian process and measurement noises: $$\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, \mathbf{w}_t), \quad \mathbf{w}_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \mathbf{Q}_t)$$ $$\mathbf{z}_t = \mathbf{h}(\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{v}_t), \quad \mathbf{v}_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \mathbf{R}_t)$$ with initial belief $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_0) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_0, \mathbf{P}_0)$.

Perform a first-order Taylor approximation of $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, \mathbf{w}_t)$ around $(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}, \mathbf{w}_t = 0)$ and of $\mathbf{h}(\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{v}_t)$ around $(\mathbf{x}_t = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, \mathbf{v}_t = 0)$: $$\mathbf{x}_t \approx \mathbf{f}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, 0) + \mathbf{F}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}) + \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{w}_t$$ $$\mathbf{z}_t \approx \mathbf{h}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, 0) + \mathbf{H}_t(\mathbf{x}_t - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}) + \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{v}_t$$ where the Jacobian matrices are defined by partial derivatives evaluated at the operating points: $$\mathbf{F}_t = \frac{\partial \mathbf{f}}{\partial \mathbf{x}_{t-1}}\bigg|_{\mathbf{x}_{t-1}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}}, \quad \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}} = \frac{\partial \mathbf{f}}{\partial \mathbf{w}_t}\bigg|_{\mathbf{x}_{t-1}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1},\, \mathbf{w}_t=0}$$ $$\mathbf{H}_t = \frac{\partial \mathbf{h}}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t}\bigg|_{\mathbf{x}_t=\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}}, \quad \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}} = \frac{\partial \mathbf{h}}{\partial \mathbf{v}_t}\bigg|_{\mathbf{x}_t=\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1},\, \mathbf{v}_t=0}$$

Expand and group terms in the linearized models into linear state terms, known deterministic offsets, and transformed zero-mean Gaussian noise terms: $$\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \tilde{\mathbf{u}}_t + \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_t$$ where $\tilde{\mathbf{u}}_t = \mathbf{f}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, 0) - \mathbf{F}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}$ and $\tilde{\mathbf{w}}_t = \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{w}_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{Q}_t\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}^{\intercal})$, and $$\mathbf{z}_t = \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t + \tilde{\mathbf{z}}_t + \tilde{\mathbf{v}}_t$$ where $\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_t = \mathbf{h}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, 0) - \mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}$ and $\tilde{\mathbf{v}}_t = \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{v}_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{R}_t\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}^{\intercal})$.

Write the resulting conditional Gaussian probability density functions for state transition and observation under the linearized models: $$p(\mathbf{x}_t | \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \tilde{\mathbf{u}}_t, \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{Q}_t\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}^{\intercal}) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\det(2\pi \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{Q}_t\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}^{\intercal})}} \exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \tilde{\mathbf{u}}_t)^{\intercal}(\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{Q}_t\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}^{\intercal})^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \tilde{\mathbf{u}}_t)\right)$$ $$p(\mathbf{z}_t | \mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t + \tilde{\mathbf{z}}_t, \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{R}_t\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}^{\intercal}) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\det(2\pi \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{R}_t\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}^{\intercal})}} \exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t - \tilde{\mathbf{z}}_t)^{\intercal}(\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{R}_t\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}^{\intercal})^{-1}(\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t - \tilde{\mathbf{z}}_t)\right)$$

Formulate the recursive Bayesian belief propagation equations for the predicted belief $\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t)$ via marginalization over $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ and the corrected belief $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_t)$ via Bayes' rule: $$\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) = \int p(\mathbf{x}_t | \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t)\,\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1})\,d\mathbf{x}_{t-1} \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1})$$ $$\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_t) = \eta \cdot p(\mathbf{z}_t | \mathbf{x}_t)\,\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t})$$

Substitute the linearized Gaussian transition density $p(\mathbf{x}_t | \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t)$ and prior belief $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}, \mathbf{P}_{t-1|t-1})$ into the prediction integral (noting that $\mathbf{F}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1} + \tilde{\mathbf{u}}_t = \mathbf{f}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, 0)$) to obtain the EKF prediction step equations (where the detailed Gaussian integral algebra is cross-referenced to Section 8 in [arxiv:2406.06427]): $$\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{f}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1|t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t, 0)$$ $$\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1|t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}} \mathbf{Q}_t \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{w}}^{\intercal}$$

Substitute the linearized Gaussian observation density $p(\mathbf{z}_t | \mathbf{x}_t)$ and predicted belief $\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1})$ into the Bayes update equation (noting that $\mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} + \tilde{\mathbf{z}}_t = \mathbf{h}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, 0)$) to obtain the EKF correction step equations (where the detailed Gaussian product and matrix inversion algebra is cross-referenced to Section 8 in [arxiv:2406.06427]): $$\mathbf{K}_t = \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal}\left(\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}} \mathbf{R}_t \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}}^{\intercal}\right)^{-1}$$ $$\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} + \mathbf{K}_t\left(\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{h}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, 0)\right)$$ $$\mathbf{P}_{t|t} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_t \mathbf{H}_t)\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}$$ (When measurement noise is additive so $\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{v}} = \mathbf{I}$, the innovation covariance reduces to $\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t$.)

For continuous-time dynamics $\dot{\mathbf{x}}(t) = f(\mathbf{x}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)) + \mathbf{w}(t)$ with $\mathbf{w}(t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{Q}(t))$ and discrete-time measurements $\mathbf{z}_k = h(\mathbf{x}_k) + \mathbf{v}_k$ with $\mathbf{v}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{R}_k)$ at $\mathbf{x}_k = \mathbf{x}(t_k)$, the prediction step solves the coupled differential equations from $t_{k-1}$ to $t_k$ with $\mathbf{F}(t) = \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial \mathbf{x}}\right|_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)}$: $$\begin{cases} \dot{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}(t) = f(\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)) \\ \dot{\mathbf{P}}(t) = \mathbf{F}(t)\mathbf{P}(t) + \mathbf{P}(t)\mathbf{F}(t)^T + \mathbf{Q}(t) \end{cases} \quad \text{with } \begin{cases} \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_{k-1}) = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1|k-1} \\ \mathbf{P}(t_{k-1}) = \mathbf{P}_{k-1|k-1} \end{cases} \implies \begin{cases} \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_k) \\ \mathbf{P}_{k|k-1} = \mathbf{P}(t_k) \end{cases}$$ followed by the identical discrete-time update equations at $t_k$, or in purely continuous time by the coupled filter equations $\dot{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}(t) = f(\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)) + \mathbf{K}(t)(\mathbf{z}(t) - h(\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t)))$ and $\dot{\mathbf{P}}(t) = \mathbf{F}(t)\mathbf{P}(t) + \mathbf{P}(t)\mathbf{F}(t)^T - \mathbf{K}(t)\mathbf{H}(t)\mathbf{P}(t) + \mathbf{Q}(t)$.

assumptions.assumption: First-order Taylor approximation accuracy: the nonlinear motion model f and observation model h are well-approximated by linear Taylor expansions around the current estimates (x_hat_{t-1|t-1}, w_t=0) and (x_hat_{t|t-1}, v_t=0).
assumptions.breaks_when: The system or measurement functions are highly nonlinear over the scale of the estimation uncertainty or noise, making higher-order Taylor terms significant.

assumptions.assumption: Well-defined differentiable transition and observation models: the Jacobians F_t, F_w, H_t, and H_v exist at the current state estimates.
assumptions.breaks_when: The motion model f or observation model h is non-differentiable or discontinuous at the linearization point.

assumptions.assumption: Gaussian distribution of random variables and beliefs: process noise w_t ~ N(0, Q_t), measurement noise v_t ~ N(0, R_t), and the state beliefs bel(x_t) are unimodal Gaussian distributions.
assumptions.breaks_when: Noise or state distributions are non-Gaussian or multimodal, or nonlinear transformations severely distort the Gaussian shape.

assumptions.assumption: Invertibility of the linearized noise and innovation covariance matrices: (F_w Q_t F_w^T), (H_v R_t H_v^T), and (H_t P_{t|t-1} H_t^T + H_v R_t H_v^T) are non-singular.
assumptions.breaks_when: The innovation covariance H_t P_{t|t-1} H_t^T + H_v R_t H_v^T (or the linearized noise covariance in the density expression) is singular or ill-conditioned.

failure_modes.mode: First-order linearization error in strongly nonlinear regimes
failure_modes.signature: Degraded state estimation accuracy or filter divergence when higher-order terms of the Taylor series expansion cannot be neglected.
failure_modes.cause: Linearizing f and h about the current mean estimate drops second- and higher-order Taylor terms (which higher-order EKFs retain).

failure_modes.mode: Singular innovation covariance in Kalman gain computation
failure_modes.signature: Matrix inversion (H_t P_{t|t-1} H_t^T + H_v R_t H_v^T)^{-1} fails or becomes numerically unstable.
failure_modes.cause: Deficient projected measurement noise covariance H_v R_t H_v^T combined with rank-deficient H_t P_{t|t-1} H_t^T.

instantiation.why_here: In `agrios_ws`, two `robot_localization` instances (`ekf_local` at 50.0 Hz and `ekf_global` at 30.0 Hz) run an Extended Kalman Filter over a 15-dimensional state vector (X, Y, Z, Roll, Pitch, Yaw, Vx, Vy, Vz, Vroll, Vpitch, Vyaw, Ax, Ay, Az). `ekf_local` fuses velocity measurements from `/odom_cov` (`odom0`) and yaw-rate measurements from `/imu` (`imu0`), while `ekf_global` additionally fuses X, Y position measurements from `/odometry/gps` (`odom1`) and Yaw orientation measurements from `/rtk/heading` (`imu1`). Both filters propagate the state error covariance using `transfer_function_jacobian_` and add `delta_sec * (*process_noise_covariance)` at each prediction step.

concrete.in_your_project: 15x1 state vector with entries X, Y, Z, Roll, Pitch, Yaw, Vx, Vy, Vz, Vroll, Vpitch, Vyaw, Ax, Ay, Az tracked by both `ekf_local` and `ekf_global`.

Measurements read from sensor topics: `/odom_cov` (`odom0`, fusing Vx, Vy, Vyaw in both filters), `/imu` (`imu0`, fusing Vyaw in both filters), `/odometry/gps` (`odom1`, fusing X, Y in `ekf_global`), and `/rtk/heading` (`imu1`, fusing Yaw in `ekf_global`).

Observation noise covariance populated inside incoming measurement messages: `odom_cov_relay` sets a 36-element (6x6) `msg.twist.covariance` on `/odom_cov` with diagonal entries `c[0] = 0.05` (vx), `c[7] = 0.05` (vy), and `c[35] = 0.02` (vyaw); `rtk_sim` sets `hdg.orientation_covariance` on `/rtk/heading` (and marks `angular_velocity_covariance[0] = -1.0` and `linear_acceleration_covariance[0] = -1.0`), as well as `fix.position_covariance` with `COVARIANCE_TYPE_DIAGONAL_KNOWN`.

15x15 diagonal `process_noise_covariance` matrix in `ekf_local.yaml` and `ekf_global.yaml`; in `src/ekf.cpp:436`, `(*process_noise_covariance)` is scaled by `delta_sec` and added to `estimate_error_covariance_`.

15x15 `transfer_function_jacobian_` in `src/ekf.cpp:436`, which pre- and post-multiplies `estimate_error_covariance_` (`transfer_function_jacobian_ * estimate_error_covariance_ * transfer_function_jacobian_.transpose()`).

15x15 `estimate_error_covariance_` on the right-hand side of `src/ekf.cpp:436`, initialized at startup from the 15x15 `initial_estimate_covariance` parameter (all 15 diagonal entries set to `1e-9`, off-diagonals zero).

15x15 `estimate_error_covariance_` after `src/ekf.cpp:436` computes `transfer_function_jacobian_ * estimate_error_covariance_ * transfer_function_jacobian_.transpose()` and adds `delta_sec * (*process_noise_covariance)`.
